sentences.text: Heard on admission.
Admit.
This case is heard finally with the consent of learned counsel for the parties.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 254 of 2025 , which is first application under Section 430(1) of B.N.S.S., 2023 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant is dismissed as withdrawn.

This appeal is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of the judgment dated 23.12.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO Act, 2012 & S.C./ S.T. Act) / Eleventh Additional Sessions Judge, in Special Sessions Case No. 139/2021 whereby the appellant has been convicted under Section 363 of IPC and sentenced to 2 years' R.I. with fine of Rs.1,000/-, Section 366 of IPC and sentenced to 3 year R.I. with fine of Rs.1,000/-, Section 3(a) r/w NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

sentences.text: Though the appellant has also been convicted under Section 376 of IPC but has not been separately sentenced.
2. The allegation against the appellant is that he kidnapped the prosecutrix, who was less than 18 years of age and forcibly committed sexual intercourse with her.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He further submits that the DNA report dated 19.01.2023 is not against the present appellant.
The prosecutrix herself has admitted in cross-examination that she used to call the accused by message on phone.
The prosecutrix was more than 18 years old at the time of alleged incident and was a consenting party.
He, therefore, prays for acquittal of the accused.
4. Learned Government Advocate supports the impugned judgment and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

He fairly admits that it is correct to say that DNA report is not positive qua appellant and inspite of X-ray advise to determine age of the prosecutrix, the same was not done and there is no birth certificate also, but learned Govt. Advocate submits that as per the statement of school teacher P.W.5 Mohd. Safique, the date of birth of the prosecutrix is 22.07.2003, hence she was a minor on the date of the incident i.e. 16.02.2021.
5.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6. On perusal of the record, it is seen that as per paragraph 36 of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:61756 3 CRA-40-2025 impugned judgment, DNA report is not positive qua appellant.

It is seen that the Investigating Officer P.W.11 Bhumeshwari Chauhan has very fairly admitted in paragraph 6 that the doctor had advised for ossification test report to determine the age of the prosecutrix but report is not filed.

7. P.W.1 - prosecutrix has stated that due to consistent and persistent pressure of the accused, he made friends with the appellant but he filled vermilion on her head and made the photographs of marriage viral.
In paragraph 15 she agreed that at the relevant time she was 17 years and 7 months old.
8. P.W.2 - mother of the prosecutrix and P.W.3 aunt of the prosecutrix have supported the prosecution case.
9. P.W.4 - Satyanarayan Kushwaha is Investigating Officer of the case.

10. P.W.5 - Mohd Safique is the Principal of the School who stated that the date of birth of the prosecutrix is 22.07.2003, but he cannot say as to on what basis the date of birth was written.
11. P.W. 7 Dr. Neelkamal Sohane has stated that there were no external injury on the body of the prosecutrix and X-Ray was advised.
It is seen that the prosecution has failed to establish by reliable evidence that on the date of the offence, prosecutrix was minor being less than 18 years of age.
DNA report is not against the appellant.

sentences.text: In view of evidence available on record and the statement of the prosecutrix, it is seen that the prosecution has failed to prove that on the date of the offence i.e. 16.02.2021, prosecutrix was minor being less than 18 years NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:61756 4 CRA-40-2025 of age.
Hence finding of the Trial Court regarding age of the prosecutrix is set aside.

Once it is held that the prosecution has failed to prove that on the date of the offence, the prosecutrix was minor then any consensual relationship between two adults would not come under the purview of criminal action.
13. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned judgment is set aside.
The appellant is acquitted of all the charges as mentioned in the impugned judgment.
14. The appellant be released from jail, if not required in any other case.
15. The disposal of the property shall be as per the judgment of the Trial Court.

(AVANINDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE VSG Harsh Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53646622/
